newsitem.title: UK: National Power wins Indonesia power deal.
newsitem.headline: National Power wins Indonesia power deal.

text.p: British utility National Power Plc said on Wednesday it had won its first major project in Indonesia as part of a consortium that plans to build a $1.6 billion coal-fired power station.

National Power said the consortium signed a 30-year power purchase agreement under which the Indonesian state-owned electricity corporation, PT PLN (PERSERO), would buy power from the 1,320 megawatt plant.
The consortium has set up an Indonesian project company, PT Tanjung Jati Power Company, in which National Power will have a stake of 30 percent for around $130 million.
Japan's Tomen Corporation will have 30 percent and two Indonesian firms -- PT Bakrie Power Corporation and PT Maharani Paramitra -- will each hold 20 percent.
National Power and Bakrie will operate the plant, which is expected to start in 2001.
